title: Hardware Remote Attestation Evidence Specification (IETF RATS RFC 9334 / DAA-ZK Anchor)
description: Formal specification for cryptographically verifiable hardware evidence conforming to the IETF Remote Attestation Procedures (RATS, RFC 9334) architecture. Enforces a bijective mapping between trusted silicon state and autonomous node identity while concealing persistent hardware identifiers via zero-knowledge Pedersen commitments.

schema_version.description: Semantic versioning string of this formal schema specification (e.g. 1.0.0).

node_id.description: EVM-standard 20-byte hexadecimal address derived from the node operational ECDSA/Ed25519 public key.

blinded_silicon_commitment.description: 32-byte Pedersen commitment Commit(Chip_Secret, r) blinding the physical silicon identifier into a zero-knowledge nullifier.

platform_pcr_digest.description: SHA-256 composite measurement digest of Platform Configuration Registers (PCR 0-7: firmware, secure boot state, and kernel integrity measurements).

ak_public_key.description: DER or PEM encoded public key of the Attestation Key (AK) generated within the trusted hardware boundary.

quote_signature.description: Hexadecimal cryptographic signature generated by the hardware AK over the quote_payload and replay-prevention nonce.

quote_payload.description: TPM2B_ATTEST or TEE hardware quote data structure encoded in base64 or hexadecimal format.

proof_type.description: Designated zero-knowledge proof or Direct Anonymous Attestation (DAA) scheme proving Root CA membership without certificate serial disclosure.

proof_bytes.description: Serialized byte array of the zero-knowledge or DAA cryptographic proof.

public_inputs.description: Public signals for circuit verification (e.g. root hash of the vendor CA Merkle accumulation tree, challenge hash).

silicon_vendor.description: Standardized hardware security architecture and isolation subsystem designation.

silicon_firmware_version.description: Reported firmware and microcode release identifier certified by the secure element.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch timestamp in seconds at the time of attestation generation.

nonce.description: 32-byte cryptographic nonce provided by the verifier to guarantee freshness and prevent replay attacks.
